title: The hospital bag
summary: What to put in the bag, in the order you will want it. Print it, tick it, and leave it by the door.

sections.title: Paperwork, first
sections.note: This is the section people forget, and the one you cannot buy at the hospital gift shop.

items.label: Photo ID and your insurance card
items.detail: Some hospitals ask for both at the desk before you go up.

items.label: Your birth preferences, on one page
items.detail: A copy for the bag and a copy for your support person. Staff change shifts.

items.label: The pediatrician's name and number
items.detail: The hospital asks who will see the baby after you leave.

items.label: A list of every medicine you take, with doses
items.detail: Include anything over the counter, and any allergies.

items.label: The car seat manual, or a photo of the label

sections.title: For labour
sections.note: You will not want most of this. Bring it anyway; someone else can fetch it.

items.label: Lip balm
items.detail: The single most recommended item on every list, and the one nobody believes.

items.label: A hair tie and a headband
Warm socks with grips
items.detail: Hospital floors are cold and you will be walking them.

items.label: A phone charger with a long cable
items.detail: Long enough to reach the bed from the wall. Six feet is not too long.

items.label: A small speaker or headphones
A tennis ball or a massage tool
items.detail: For your back, held by your support person.

items.label: Snacks and a water bottle with a straw
items.detail: Ask your team what you can eat. Some hospitals limit food in labour.

sections.title: For after the birth
sections.note: You will be in a room, in a gown, for a day or more. These are the things that make that easier.

items.label: A dark robe or a loose nightgown
items.detail: Dark, because of what happens to light fabric.

items.label: High-waisted underwear you do not mind losing
items.detail: Two sizes up. A cesarean scar sits where a waistband sits.

items.label: Heavy pads, unscented
items.detail: The hospital supplies some. Bring your own for the ride home.

items.label: Toothbrush, toothpaste, and a hairbrush
Flip-flops for the shower
Clothes to go home in that fit at seven months pregnant
items.detail: Your body is not back to its usual size on day two, and that is not a problem to solve.

items.label: Your own pillow, in a case you can tell apart
Lanolin or nipple cream

sections.title: For the baby
sections.note: The hospital has most of this. What it does not have is the car seat.

items.label: The car seat, installed, with the base
items.detail: The hospital will not let you leave in a car without one. Install it before week 36.

items.label: One outfit to go home in, in newborn size
items.detail: One. Not four. Bring the next size up as well, because newborn is a guess.

items.label: A blanket for the car
A hat and socks
A soft nail file
items.detail: Newborn nails are sharp and scissors are a bad idea in a hospital chair.

sections.title: For your support person
sections.note: They are there for a long time and nobody packs for them.

items.label: A change of clothes and a toothbrush
Food that does not need a fridge
items.detail: Cafeterias close. Vending machines do not take a card at 3am in every hospital.

items.label: Small bills and a card
items.detail: Parking, and the vending machine.

items.label: A pillow and a blanket
items.detail: The chair folds out. It is not a bed.

items.label: A notebook and a pen
items.detail: For what the nurses tell you at 4am, which you will not remember.

sections.title: In the car, not in the bag
sections.note: Leave these in the car now, so the ride home is not the first time you think about them.

items.label: The car seat, checked against the manual
items.detail: The seat does not move more than an inch at the belt path. The chest clip sits at armpit height.

items.label: A blanket for the baby's legs
items.detail: Over the buckled harness, never under it.

items.label: A bag with a change of clothes and a towel
